stories.standfirst: It came down to the very last season, and in the end {winner} found the answer that {loser} could not quite take away.
paragraphs: Some Showdowns are decided early and some are decided late. This one waited for its final season, and only then did {winner} move clear to finish with {winnerPoints}, leaving {loser} on {loserPoints} when the book closed.
That final season carried the weight of all the others. {winnerClub} and {loserClub} had been inseparable for long stretches, and the margin of {margin} was only fixed at the very last moment.
Nobody will remember the quiet years as clearly as this one. The final page is always the longest.

pullquote.text: The last season arrived with everything still undecided, and it did not disappoint.

stories.standfirst: Every point mattered until the last, and the last of them belonged to {winner}, who edged home by {margin}.
paragraphs: The ledger stayed open to the end. Across {seasonsTotal} seasons the lead had never felt safe for either manager, and only the final season could say who would take the Showdown. It said {winner}, with {winnerPoints} against {loserPoints}.
A margin of {margin} sounds small written down. In a race this long it is the gap between a trophy and a long walk home, and {winnerClub} has crossed it.
Close the books and read the total once more. It will not change, however many times you look.

pullquote.text: A small margin on paper can be a very large one in the heart.

stories.standfirst: Never has a rivalry made so much of its final chapter, as {winner} held on when {loser} pushed hardest.
paragraphs: There was no champion until there was nothing left to play. {loser} pressed {winner} through the closing season, and the rivalry ran to its limit before {winner} finished ahead on the overall count.
That is the character of this contest. {winnerClub} and {loserClub} kept each other honest from the first season to the last, and the margin of {margin} is what honesty looks like in print.
The next rivalry will have to work hard to match this one.

pullquote.text: A race this tight has no winner until the very end, and no loser worth pitying.

stories.standfirst: Hold the front page, because the Showdown was not settled until the final season, and then it was settled by {winner}.
paragraphs: Up to the very last moment the Gazette kept two headlines ready. When the final season ended, {winner} had {winnerPoints}, {loser} had {loserPoints} and only one of the prepared pages went to print.
Close finishes are the stuff of memory. {winnerClub} will remember the nerve it took, and {loserClub} will remember how near the distance was, with only {margin} between them at the death.
Late editions are rarely so well rewarded. Tonight the wait was worth every minute.

pullquote.text: We kept two headlines ready and only one of them was needed.

stories.standfirst: The archive will mark this Showdown as one that lived until the last page, and then quietly gave itself to {winner}.
paragraphs: Some contests are won in the middle and merely confirmed at the end. This was not one of them. Over {seasonsTotal} seasons, {winner} and {loser} stayed so close that only the final season could draw a line between them.

{winnerClub} finished on {winnerPoints} and {loserClub} on {loserPoints}. The difference is a modest {margin}, but modest distances make the finest stories, and this one is already filed under favourites.
Archivists love a late twist. This one will be pulled from the shelf often.

pullquote.text: The best files are the ones where the last page changes everything.

stories.standfirst: Everything before it was preparation, because the final season was the one that decided who would claim the Showdown.
paragraphs: For {seasonsTotal} seasons the contest held its breath. Then the last of them arrived, and {winner} gathered enough to pass {loser} and take the Showdown, finishing on {winnerPoints} against {loserPoints}.
It is a rare achievement to be best at the moment that matters most. {winnerClub} was exactly that, while {loserClub} gave the closing season everything it had, and left {margin} short of the line.
That is the beauty of waiting. The ending felt earned because nobody could see it coming.

pullquote.text: You cannot win a long race early, only on the last page.

stories.standfirst: Down at {winnerClub} the celebrations will be late, because the Showdown was only decided at the end of the very last season.
paragraphs: Nobody at {winnerClub} was able to relax until the final points were counted. {winner} spent the whole of the closing season in the chase, and the reward is a Showdown title with a margin of {margin} over {loser}.
At {loserClub} the sense of a near thing will last longer than the season did. A contest decided at the final hurdle is the cruellest and the finest kind, and both managers gave it all they had.
Some wins are loud. This one was breathless.

pullquote.text: We counted the points three times and then we sat down.
pullquote.who: The tea lady at the training ground

stories.standfirst: The longest campaign in the book has ended, and the winner of the Showdown was only known at the final turn.
paragraphs: The Gazette has watched {seasonsTotal} seasons pass, and none of them gave away the ending. Only the last season did that, and it handed the Showdown to {winner} with {winnerPoints} on the board.
There is no shame in the chase. {loser} finished on {loserPoints}, a margin of {margin} from the prize, and the rivalry has rarely been better advertised than by that closing run.
Late glory tastes best, so we are told. Tonight {winner} is in a position to confirm it.

pullquote.text: A winner who is not sure until the end has truly won.
